ops.title: synckit 0.37 rejects only service.socket — this laptop's three manifests were pre-0.31 stale, already fatal under 0.36, and the machine is now dormant by intent
ops.body:
`synckitd` on `yasyf-forge` went 0.36.4 → 0.37.1 and loaded none of its three
manifests. The obvious reading — "0.37 broke the 0.36 manifest schema" — is
wrong, and this record exists mainly to stop the next reader adopting it.

Every claim below was re-verified on 2026-08-08 against the working tree, the
git history, the archived files, and the live peer.

## What the 0.36 → 0.37 cut actually removes: one field

Diffing `manifest/manifest.go` at `v0.36.4` against the current tree, the whole
schema delta is the deletion of `ServiceSpec.Socket`:

```go
// v0.36.4
type ServiceSpec struct {
	Kind              string `json:"kind"`
	Socket            string `json:"socket,omitempty"`
	SchemaFingerprint string `json:"schema_fingerprint"`
}
// current
type ServiceSpec struct {
	Kind              string `json:"kind"`
	SchemaFingerprint string `json:"schema_fingerprint"`
}
```

`WatchSpec` was already `{Debounce}` alone at v0.36.4 — no `backend`. `HelperSpec`
was already `{Command, SessionType}` — no `label`. There was already no `launchd`
block. So a genuine 0.36-era manifest that omits `service.socket` loads unchanged
under 0.37.

That is not theoretical. The peer `yasyf-home` (still `synckitd version 0.36.3`)
carries two manifests, and both are already on the current shape:

```
cookiesync.json → "kind", "schema_fingerprint"
reposync.json   → "kind", "schema_fingerprint"
```

Neither carries `socket`, so neither would be rejected by 0.37. **The briefed
claim that 0.37 rejects "every 0.36-era manifest" is false.** The accurate
statement is narrower: 0.37 rejects a manifest still carrying `service.socket`.

## What actually rejected this laptop's three manifests: years of drift, not 0.37

The three files were archived to
`~/.claude/state-snapshot/2026-08-07/synckit-manifests/` and removed from
`~/.config/synckit/manifests` (that directory no longer exists). Their field sets,
read out of the archive:

| file | fields present |
|---|---|
| `cc-pool.json` | `watch.backend`, `service.{transport,serve_args,sock}` |
| `reposync.json` | `watch.backend`, `service.{transport,serve_args}` |
| `cookiesync.json` | `service.{transport,serve_args,sock}`, `helper.label`, `launchd{}` |

None of those fields survived into 0.36. Dating each removal by the commit that
deleted it and the first tag containing it:

- `watch.backend` — `e386be4` (2026-07-13), first in **v0.10.0**
- `helper.label` / the `launchd` block — `67f73b7` (2026-07-20), first in **v0.24.0**
  (CHANGELOG 0.30.0 calls them "the unused manifest `launchd`/helper-label fields")
- `service.{transport,serve_args}` — `1dfff0f` (2026-07-23), first in **v0.31.0**

So these manifests were stale by six to twenty-seven minor releases, and not one
of them was rejected by anything 0.37 did.

`manifest.Load` sets `decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()` (`manifest/manifest.go:122`),
which reports the *first* unknown key in document order. Walking each archived
file's key order reproduces the observed errors exactly:

- `cc-pool.json` → `watch.backend` is the first unknown → `unknown field "backend"`
- `reposync.json` → same → `unknown field "backend"`
- `cookiesync.json` → has no `backend`; first unknown is `service.transport` → `unknown field "transport"`

which matches what was reported at the time. The error messages were right; the
attribution to 0.37 was not.

## These manifests were already fatal under 0.36.4

This is the part that reframes the incident. At `v0.36.4`, `manifest.Discover`
returned on the first bad file:

```go
m, err := Load(filepath.Join(dir, name))
if err != nil {
	return nil, err
}
```

One unloadable manifest failed the entire scan. 0.37.0 is what *changed* that —
it skips the file, logs the offending field, and returns a `[]manifest.Skipped`
so `synckitd status` can name the stale consumer. So on the evidence the laptop's
manifest scan was already broken before the upgrade, and 0.37 turned a fatal scan
into a diagnosable one. (Derived from v0.36.4 source; not observed live on this
machine before the upgrade.)

## Resolution on this machine — dormant by intent, not broken

The user chose to leave synckit **dormant** on `yasyf-forge` and registered no
consumers. The three stale manifests were archived (never deleted — per the
archive-never-delete rule in daemonkit doc `f2ec2cb`) and removed from
`~/.config/synckit/manifests`.

Current observed state:

```
$ synckitd status
self:   yasyf@yasyf-forge.tail71af5d.ts.net
host:   yasyf@yasyf-home.tail71af5d.ts.net
label:  com.github.yasyf.synckit.serve
daemon: not running
```

`daemon: not running` here is **joined-but-idle by intent**, not a fault. Anyone
finding this machine should not "repair" it by re-registering consumers.

Installed consumer versions on this laptop, for whoever does decide to re-register:
`cc-pool v0.64.9`, `cookiesync 0.27.4`, `reposync 0.27.5`. Manifests cannot be
hand-written — `Validate` requires `service.schema_fingerprint` to bind the exact
service schema via `syncservice.ValidateServiceSchema` (`manifest/manifest.go:102-103`)
— so regeneration means re-running each consumer's own install command, then
`synckitd install`.

Manifests are per-machine, so none of this reaches `yasyf-home`.

## f2ec2cb compliance check — honest verdict: two legs of three

Fleet doc `f2ec2cb` (daemonkit) sets the standing rule verbatim:

> **Never ship a schema/protocol hard cut without**: a migration path (or an
> explicit, documented recreate procedure), a CHANGELOG entry, and an upgrade note.

Checked, not assumed:

- **Recreate procedure — PRESENT** for 0.36→0.37. `CHANGELOG.md:72-83` carries a
  `### Migration` block: *"**Every consumer must re-register its manifest.** …
  Re-run each tool's own install command (`reposync install`, `cookiesync install`,
  `cc-pool install`, …), then `synckitd install`. `synckitd status` lists what
  loaded and what was skipped, with the offending field for each."*
- **CHANGELOG entry — PRESENT.** `## [0.37.0]` has both a `### Removed` entry for
  `manifest.ServiceSpec.Socket` and the `### Migration` block above.
- **Upgrade note — ABSENT.** There is no `UPGRADING.md` and no migration prose
  anywhere in the tree (`docs/` contains only `assets/`); `README.md` says nothing
  about upgrading or re-registering. `v0.37.0` has **no GitHub Release object at
  all** (the release run died on its `linux_arm64` build — see note `9edab95`),
  and `v0.37.1`'s release body is only a `**Full Changelog**: …compare…` link. So
  a user upgrading via Homebrew gets no upgrade note on any surface.

Two further gaps the check surfaced:

1. `### Migration` appears **exactly once** in the whole CHANGELOG — at line 72,
   under 0.37.0. The three earlier manifest cuts that actually rejected this
   laptop's files (v0.10.0, v0.24.0, v0.31.0) each shipped with **no** migration
   section. f2ec2cb names "synckit manifest model" as one of the three products
   that violated this rule; that violation is these earlier cuts, and it remains
   undocumented. 0.37.0 is the first cut that complied.
2. 0.37.0's Migration text describes the break as `service.socket` only, which is
   correct for 0.36→0.37 but will mislead anyone arriving from an older release —
   the exact failure mode that produced the wrong diagnosis recorded above.

## Open question for the owner

Given that the only surface a Homebrew upgrader sees is the release body, and
that this repo's one Migration block is reachable only by reading `CHANGELOG.md`
in the source tree: should a schema hard cut in synckit be required to ship an
upgrade note on a user-visible surface (a populated GitHub Release body, or an
`UPGRADING.md` the release body links), rather than a CHANGELOG subsection alone?
And should `synckitd status` — which since 0.37.0 already knows the offending
field per skipped consumer — say the recreate command outright, so the machine
tells the user what to run instead of the CHANGELOG doing it?
